title: AEGS Policy
description: A versioned, declarative statement of what an implementation will permit. AEGS requires that policy be identifiable and content-addressed, not that it use any particular rule language: two implementations may express the same intent very differently, and a crosswalk between them is a policy question rather than a schema one. The content hash is what makes a silent rule edit detectable, which is the property an auditor actually needs.

version.description: A content hash is strongly preferred over a label. Labels can be reused across edited rules; hashes cannot.

supersedes.description: The policy version this replaces. A policy history with the superseded versions removed is not a history.

priority.description: Lower is evaluated first where an implementation orders rules. Null where it does not.

condition.description: Human-readable. AEGS does not specify a rule language, so this is documentation rather than an executable form.

envelopes.description: Names of the BudgetEnvelopes this policy relies on.
